summary: Correct the second nkito citation from 115/137 to 115/138.
rationale: Supplied 115/137 has active gnokət; 115/138 has the quoted nkito result predicate.

summary: New box Infectum: example for sense 1 in Infectum (Jan 2.18/3749)

data.turoyo: ʕAs əno, kubaʕ d mdagalno u xabrayḏox! Qay lə kuḏaʕnox, hawxayo, bas i maǧburiye i iḏo d lə kmənkoto kmənšoqo!"
data.translation: 'As for me, do I want to contradict your statement? Why, do I not know you? That is how it is, but compulsion, the hand that cannot be bitten is kissed!'

rationale: New I Detransitive Infectum box; agentless hand patient in a proverb.

summary: New sense 2: (von Steinen und Mörtel) ineinandergreifen, aneinander haften

data.gloss: (von Steinen und Mörtel) ineinandergreifen, aneinander haften

rationale: Two construction descriptions have nonanimate material subjects and reciprocal ḥḏoḏe, with mechanical grip rather than tooth action. One technical sense groups both.

summary: New sense 1: (Detrans.) angebissen sein
rationale: Makes explicit the sense already represented by inherited nkito angebissen; no new finite Detransitive paradigm is claimed.

summary: example for sense 2 in Infectum (MAC Ishaq Material culture/72)

data.turoyo: Hənnək gnŭkti ḥḏoḏe, ṣaṭlo dəčmənto ŭ kefo, ṣaṭlo dəčmənto ŭ kefo, e.
data.translation: They’ll hold onto (lit. ‘bite’) each other, a bucket of cement and stone, a bucket of cement and stone, right.

rationale: First technical sense-2 example with mortar and stone as mutually gripping materials.

summary: example for sense 2 in Infectum (MAC Ishaq old houses/66)

data.turoyo: Gmoṭǝlle kefe, dkənne nqiwe, hawxa dlanne kefe ṭowe, kefe nqiwe, ḥariwe, laǧan dzubṭi ḥḏoḏe, kefe hawxa dnukti ḥḏoḏe.
data.translation: They would bring stones for it, which are pierced, like, the ones that are not good stones, pierced stones, destroyed ones, so that they catch one another, such stones that ‘bite’ each other.

rationale: Independent technical sense-2 attestation with rough stone subjects; same construction across two recordings.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (MAC NE Interview 2/191)

data.turoyo: Ăḷo bu+lalyo+ḥreno, lu+dewo nkətle tre, arwonk̇o ŭ tərto, me diḏan, bramšəl mdarmníwayla.
data.translation: Gosh, last night a wolf bit two (animals), a calf and a cow, of ours, last night they treated the latter.

rationale: Preterit sense 1 has three examples; explicit l-marked animal actor and quantified patient.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (57/64)

data.turoyo: Komər mədle u ḥabušawo, nkətle gazze mu ḥabušawo, xile
data.translation: Er nahm den Apfel, biß ein Stück davon ab und aß es.

rationale: Fifth Preterit sense-1 example: portion as object and apple as m- source; demonstrates ordinary bite-off construction.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (PrS 12/18)

data.turoyo: Hulele u zəbbo, knukatle u čalkoyo. Lo koṯe mede l feme. U kačal omər: “ḥete li nuro,” - məlle lu čalkoyo.
data.translation: Er gab ihm das Glied, und der Jezîdi biss darauf, aber er konnte nichts Essbares abbeissen. »Lege ihn an's Feuer«, riet ihm der Grindkopf.

rationale: Sparse Infectum: indexed object and explicit postverbal actor; unusual knukat- vocalism retained.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (PrS 18/28)

data.turoyo: Hol ṣafro lo koṯele šanto, knukatla w knušaqla w kquraṣla.
data.translation: Bis zum Morgen floh ihn der Schlaf; er biss sie, küsste sie und kniff sie;

rationale: Sparse Infectum: repeated biting with feminine patient suffix, coordinated with kissing and pinching.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (PrS 78/82)

data.turoyo: Kla zalṭoniṯo, ayna d ʕobər, knəktole w kḥənqole. Lo ṭralle ḥakime b dukṯo d lo mamṭalle l riša w lo maniḥulle.
data.translation: nackt sass sie da, und wer zu ihr in's Zimmer trat, den biss sie und erwürgte sie. Von allen Orten berief man die Aerzte zu ihr, aber umsonst.

rationale: Sparse Infectum: generic relative antecedent resumed by -le with feminine actor.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (115/137)

data.turoyo: gəzzeyo, ksoləq, xəd saləq u lalyo qamoyo, kšote mam maye w gnokət u ḥabušawo nkatto
data.translation: Er geht, er steigt hinauf wie das vorige Mal, trinkt von dem Wasser, beißt ein Stück von dem Apfel ab

rationale: Fifth Infectum sense-1 example: prospective/narrative g- and cognate nkatto alongside the bitten apple.

summary: example for sense 1 in Part. Pass. (115/134)

data.turoyo: Ṣafro qayimo, koḥayro: i šarbke dam maye noquṣto yo, u ḥabušayḏa nkito yo.
data.translation: Als die am Morgen aufstand, schaute sie: in dem Wasserkrügle in ist das Wasser weniger geworden, ihr Apfel ist angebissen.

rationale: Replaces a bare participial lemma with a self-contained result-state context for the already cited verse; no new Part. Pass. form.

summary: Sense 1: revise the gloss
rationale: Widen round-1 Detransitive sense 1 from result state to its finite event counterpart, now attested with kmənkoto.

summary: New idiom: nkətle/nokət lišono 'sich auf die Zunge beißen, verstummen'

data.headword: nkətle/nokət lišono 'sich auf die Zunge beißen, verstummen'
data.turoyo: Baʕ nkətte lišonayye. D uḏaʕwo, alfo buġre gədmuḥanwo bu tarʕo du ḥəmmam, aḏiʕət! Maʕnata, man we d haǧəm? Marke muḥetuwo, m tamo nošo, d moḥe latwo?
data.translation: Then they bit their tongues. Had they known, they would have fired a thousand bullets into the bathhouse door, you know! That means, who was it who attacked? You were shooting from here; was there nobody there to shoot?

rationale: Possessed tongue object in argumentative context supports figurative silence; single attestation, lookup of nkətte lišonayye found no existing phrase.

summary: New idiom: i iḏo d lə kmənkoto kmənšoqo 'die Hand, die man nicht beißen kann, küsst man'

data.headword: i iḏo d lə kmənkoto kmənšoqo 'die Hand, die man nicht beißen kann, küsst man'
data.turoyo: ʕAs əno, kubaʕ d mdagalno u xabrayḏox! Qay lə kuḏaʕnox, hawxayo, bas i maǧburiye i iḏo d lə kmənkoto kmənšoqo!"
data.translation: 'As for me, do I want to contradict your statement? Why, do I not know you? That is how it is, but compulsion, the hand that cannot be bitten is kissed!'

rationale: Compulsion plus paired agentless biting/kissing predicates forms a proverb about submission; mənkoto search found no existing match. Same attestation as the new box, not independent evidence.

summary: Preterit actors may be l-marked and agree with l-suffixes; patients can be bare NPs or suffixes. Body-part objects at 7/6 contrast with Maryam plus m-foṯo in the inherited elicitation.
Feminine-agent nkətla and assimilated nkətte must be interpreted in context; the same surface tt sequence is not evidence for plural agents by itself.
Infectum supports iteration, generic visitor-biting and g-prefixed narrative action. Part. Pass. nkito predicates an affected object’s result and supplies evidence of an unseen biter.
The reciprocal material construction is a technical metaphor; no actual mouth or animal actor is present. Both recordings support the same mechanical meaning.
No new evidence resolves the inherited question whether III mankatle/mankət belongs etymologically with biting. Its gloss and malformed inherited note are preserved as supplied.
The existing Detransitive box had no numbered sense list. Detransitive 1 explicitly labels its inherited result-state meaning without inventing a finite form.
Jan does not add a new active bite sense; tongue biting in an argument is a collocation with one attestation.
Finite I Detransitive kmənkoto adds an event counterpart to round-1 nkito result state. The proverb coordinates two patient-oriented predicates and omits the agent.
The modal cannot interpretation of lə kmənkoto comes from the compulsion/proverb setting, with no separate possibility morpheme on the verb. The supplied English is retained as machine translation.
No new evidence settles inherited III etymology or affects round-1 material-interlocking sense 2.
Verify PrS 73/48 nqədle against the edition or recording before admitting it as a dialectal nkt form.
At 95/204 does feminine -ayḏa in qamčkayḏa refer to the male rider’s nape, or is it a source pronominal error? No silent correction is made.
MAC NE Mor Barsaumo/8 narrates biting, whereas /15 denies any bite or wound. Is the earlier statement an impression corrected by the miraculous outcome?
Does the material-interlocking use extend beyond reciprocal construction descriptions?
Retain the editors’ inherited etymological question about III mankatle; ordinary biting evidence does not settle it.

Confirm that nkətte lišonayye at Jan 2.5/1220 conventionally expresses falling silent rather than literal tongue biting; the idiomatic interpretation is supported by the argument context but has one attestation.
Correct “loss” to “los”.
rationale: The particle in auf jemanden loslassen is los, with one s. The supplied edition likewise reads “auf sie los”.

summary: Food and body parts can be direct bitten objects; a portion can be the object with food as m- source, and nkatto can specify the bite. No separate bite-off sense is needed.
Wolves, dogs, fleas, humans and a mare are ordinary biting actors; the affected whole person may be implicit when a possessed body part is the object.
